> This notebook estimates the amount of paper needed to produce this edition of
> Micromégas and identify the most cost-effective source.



# Evaluating purchase options

Talas has some purchase options, but the most cost-effective is to buy single
sheets directly from Mohawk.



<img src="figure/purchase_options_plot-1.png" alt="" style="display: block; margin: auto;" />



Each book requires 10 sheets including two sheets for made
endpapers. Each page of text requires a pass, each chapter heading requires a
pass with red ink, and I've budgeted five passes for the title page.



| sheet|passes          | pass count|
|-----:|:---------------|----------:|
|     1|11-12-iv        |          3|
|     2|9-10-TP         |          7|
|     3|1-2-7-8-i-iii   |          6|
|     4|3-4-5-6-ii      |          5|
|     5|13-14-27-v      |          4|
|     6|15-16-25-26     |          4|
|     7|17-18-23-24-vi  |          5|
|     8|19-20-21-22-vii |          5|
|     9|EP1             |          0|
|    10|EP2             |          0|





If we estimate spoilage of 1 sheet per book plus 1--2 sheets per pass, the cost
of paper per book is well under \$1.50.

<img src="figure/paper_estimates_plot-1.png" alt="" style="display: block; margin: auto;" />

# Actual purchase

40 × Mohawk Superfine, smooth, white, 80-pound text (118 GSM), 25×38″



Each sheet of stock paper yields 15 print-ready sheets after cutting -- enough
for 60 books with no spoilage. In practice, I'm aiming for an edition of 50 with
a stretch goal of 55.

<img src="figure/paper_plan_plot-1.png" alt="" style="display: block; margin: auto;" />

The following table budgets all 600 sheets of cut stock to produce 55
books, with extra spoilage distributed proportionally to the number of passes
each sheet requires.
